title: What if you lit a candle in space?
caption:
In space, fire is round. 🕯️🛰️

On Earth, hot air rises and drags a candle flame into a yellow teardrop full of glowing soot. In orbit nothing is "up": hot air can't rise, so oxygen only creeps in by diffusion and the flame becomes a small, soot-free blue ball (about 1.5 cm across in NASA's Space Shuttle tests).

It also burns slowly: candles that last 10 minutes or less on Earth kept a flame for up to 45 minutes on the Mir space station. The wax doesn't drip; it melts into a liquid ball.

The twist: when the flame goes out, a white cloud of wax vapour 2–3 times the flame's size keeps drifting, and it is still flammable. That's why NASA studies fire in orbit so carefully.
